classification.difficultyReason: Handle an absolute value and solve two quadratic equations in cosine while enforcing its nonnegative value.

answer.short:
$\theta=0,\dfrac\pi3,\dfrac{5\pi}3,2\pi$.

Use $\cos2\theta=2\cos^2\theta-1$ and consider both signs of the absolute value.
answer.worked:
Since $|\cos2\theta|\ge0$, we need $\cos\theta\ge0$. Let $c=\cos\theta$, so $0\le c\le1$ and $c=|2c^2-1|$.

If $2c^2-1\ge0$,
$$\begin{align*}c&=2c^2-1\\2c^2-c-1&=0\\(2c+1)(c-1)&=0\\c&=1\end{align*}$$

The root $c=-\tfrac12$ is excluded by $c\ge0$.

If $2c^2-1<0$,
$$\begin{align*}c&=1-2c^2\\2c^2+c-1&=0\\(2c-1)(c+1)&=0\\c&=\frac12\end{align*}$$

The root $c=-1$ is excluded by $c\ge0$. The retained roots satisfy their respective sign conditions.

$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta=1:&\quad\theta=0,2\pi\\\cos\theta=\frac12:&\quad\theta=\frac\pi3,\frac{5\pi}3\end{align*}$$

Therefore $\theta=0,\tfrac\pi3,\tfrac{5\pi}3,2\pi$.
